7 months FCI Loretto in PA, spent 4 days in the SHU when I first got there. EVERYONE gets a few days in the SHU upon arrival, they tell ya it's because they're waiting for a bed in gen-pop, but I'm pretty sure it's just to give you a taste of where you go when you break the rules...it's most commonly used as punishment (get caught with tobacco=30 days, etc), though some guys voluntarily go there if they have "problems" in gen-pop, like another inmate (or group of inmates) wants to bash your head in and you're scared.

It's NOT solitary confinement. The cells all have bunk beds, and at times there were three to a cell with a mattress thrown on the floor. It's NOT a nice place, you spend all but one hour a day in a tiny brick-walled room with the bunk bed, a stainless steel toilet, and a "desk" that's just a steel shelf with an attached stool that swivels out from underneath. Your food is delivered through a slot in the door three times a day...same food the guys in gen-pop eat, but cold by the time it gets to you. Your allowed one book, a little rubber pen, and a sheet of paper to write a letter on. It can REALLY suck if you get a bad cellmate, I was lucky...got some quiet black dude who spent his days exercising, reading, and sleeping. He was big on the exercise...he calculated the distance of walking across the cell into a mile, like 700 trips back and forth was the equivalent of one mile. Yeah...that was a bit annoying, but it was better than having him rape me or shank me (or both).

As you see in the attached pic, there are steel bars on the bed frame, and you get real sheets (not these "paper" ones they keep talking about) that you could fashion into a noose. You COULD kill yourself in a SHU cell...obviously I had no desire to off myself with a 7 month stretch, but it could be done. That's one of the reasons there are two to a cell, they figure your cellmate isn't gonna sit there and watch you kill himself...for one thing he sure as fuck doesn't wanna get blamed for your death.

Now the orange jumpsuit thing. I saw a lot of people piping up on that one, the common conception being that everyone wears khaki or dark green "Dickey-style" uniforms. At Loretta, we wore the green ones at mealtimes, for classes, and your work detail (some places use the khaki/tan color ones). Rest of the time it was grey sweats and t-shirts that you bought in commissary. However, you wore an orange jumpsuit in the SHU, usually very old and faded, and several sizes too large. The other pic attached shows some guys in a SHU unit cage, a little box they put you in whenever you aren't in your cell for some reason...you can clearly see the guys are wearing these baggy orange clown suits.
